description: Follows Mansa Musa’s 1324 pilgrimage through the Mali Empire’s political, religious and commercial networks. Examines Sundiata’s legacy, gold production and coerced labor, Cairo diplomacy and reported gold-price changes, Timbuktu’s longer scholarly history, and the distinct perspectives of oral traditions, travelers and the Catalan Atlas.

period.label: c. 1312–1337 CE · reign of Mansa Musa
period.note: The manuscript places accession around 1312 and death in the 1330s, often around 1337. This is the approximate reign, not a lifespan or the duration of Mali. The pilgrimage is dated 1324–probably 1325; Ibn Battuta’s 1352–1353 visit, the 1375 atlas and later scholarly flourishing are separate evidence and context.
